sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northwest corner of the old Fair Lawn village around the junction of River Road and Bergen Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Bergen Avenue crosses the sheet from west to east about two thirds of the way down, and Fairlawn Avenue runs along the bottom edge (its south side is on sheet 3). River Road enters from the northwest as a broad curve and turns south across Bergen Avenue; First Street (today 6th Street) runs along the west edge. North of Bergen Avenue, Campbell Road leaves River Road and climbs northeast past Raymond Street to George Street, with the lettered lots of the J. De Beeman Map on either side of it. Raymond Street and the northern George Street are lined with rows of one- and one-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings with garages; George Street jogs at Bergen Avenue, so its southern stretch lies about 120 feet west of the northern one. South of Bergen Avenue the Fairlawn Homes Co. Map subdivision fills the block between First Street and River Road, with a concrete-block garage for ten cars at its north end, a few brick stores on Fairlawn Avenue, and dwellings drawn 'from plans' on Bergen Avenue. A filling station stands on River Road at the northwest. Along the east edge runs the abandoned right of way of the North Jersey Rapid Transit, now followed by Parmelee Avenue. Large parts of blocks 118 to 120 and 131 to 132 are still vacant. Water pipes of 6 to 16 inches are drawn along the streets.
notes: Old First Street is today's 6th Street; the old street numbers ran westward from River Road (1st to 5th), the modern ones run eastward from the Passaic (2nd to 6th).
The North Jersey Rapid Transit right of way (abandoned) along the east edge is now roughly Parmelee Avenue.
George Street jogs about 120 ft at Bergen Avenue; the two OpenStreetMap junction nodes 30 m apart were both detected.
Campbell Road is drawn on a slightly different line from the modern road between Raymond and George Streets; its junction with George Street was not detected.

50 ft. River Rd / Bergen Av, Campbell Rd, Raymond St, George St (jogs ~120 ft at Bergen Av), First St (= modern 6th St) on west edge, Fairlawn Av at bottom; abandoned North Jersey Rapid Transit right of way on east edge (now Parmelee Av). One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the business centre of the old Fair Lawn village between Fairlawn Avenue (north) and Hopper Avenue (south), from First Street (today 6th Street) on the west to Edward Street on the east, at 50 feet to an inch. River Road runs north-south through the middle and is the commercial frontage: on its west side stand brick stores, a hardware and paint store, a drug store, the Kuiken Lumber Co. with scattered lumber and a lumber storage shed, and the house of the Fairlawn Volunteer Fire Ass'n No. 3 with its alarm. On the east side a bank site is marked at the Fairlawn Avenue corner and a lumber storage building and a concrete-based greenhouse stand in the middle of the block. The block between First Street and River Road is lettered as part of the Fairlawn Land Improvement Association Map, and the blocks east of River Road carry the lot numbering of other subdivision maps (blocks 128 and 129). East of River Road, George and Edward Streets are lined with small frame dwellings and garages on narrow lots; Edward Street is drawn 40 feet wide, the others 50. Fairlawn Avenue is 66 feet wide west of River Road and narrower to the east. Water pipes of 6 to 16 inches are drawn in every street.
notes: Old First Street is today's 6th Street.
Kuiken Lumber Co. and the Fairlawn Volunteer Fire Ass'n No. 3 are on River Road.
Edward Street is drawn 40 ft wide, narrower than its modern right of way.
50 ft. Village centre: Fairlawn Av to Hopper Av, First St (= 6th St), River Rd, George St, Edward St; Kuiken Lumber, fire house. One part; pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the blocks west of River Road between Bergen Avenue and Fairlawn Avenue and the north half of the next row south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. From west to east the cross streets are Fifth, Fourth, Third, Second and First Streets (today 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th Streets); Fifth Street north of Fairlawn Avenue is marked 'Not opened'. Along the top, north of Bergen Avenue, the sheet shows the frontage of block 118 with scattered dwellings, a store with a milk house and a hay and feed store, and the Bergen Av. Public School (heated by steam, lit by electricity), with a garage for five cars further east. Between Bergen and Fairlawn Avenues the blocks are laid out in uniform 25-foot lots of the Fairlawn Homes Co. Map, built up with small frame dwellings and garages, except the westernmost block, which is still vacant. South of Fairlawn Avenue the Fairlawn Land Improvement Association Map continues, with a few brick dwellings, and at the corner of First Street the Kuiken Lumber Co. planing mill (concrete block with brick facing) and its raised lumber shed. Fairlawn Avenue is drawn 66 feet wide and the numbered streets 50 feet. The lower edge runs into sheet 5.
notes: Old First to Fifth Streets are today's 6th to 2nd Streets (numbering reversed).
Fifth Street (modern 2nd Street) north of Fairlawn Avenue is marked 'Not opened'; it has no junction with Bergen Avenue today either.
Bergen Av. Public School; Kuiken Lumber Co. planing mill at Fairlawn Avenue and First Street.
50 ft. Bergen Av to Fairlawn Av and south, old Fifth..First Sts (= modern 2nd..6th Sts); Fifth St north of Fairlawn "not opened"; Bergen Av Public School. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 continues sheet 4 southward and shows the blocks on both sides of Hopper Avenue west of River Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The cross streets are, from west to east, Fifth, Fourth, Third, Second and First Streets (today 2nd to 6th Streets); the drawn area ends at a line some 400 feet south of Hopper Avenue, and the lower third of the sheet is blank apart from fragments of buildings belonging to sheet 11. The lots are 25 feet wide and part of the Fairlawn Land Improvement Association Map. Building is sparse: one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, sheds and coops, a few brick dwellings, a concrete-block dwelling and a small brick silk weaving shop with an electric motor and pilastered walls on Hopper Avenue at Second Street. South of Hopper Avenue most lots are still vacant. All streets are drawn 50 feet wide, with 6-inch water pipes.
notes: Old First to Fifth Streets are today's 6th to 2nd Streets.
Silk weaving shop on Hopper Avenue at Second Street (modern 5th Street).
Only Hopper Avenue junctions are drawn, all on one line, so the part is placed with a helmert transformation.
50 ft. Both sides of Hopper Av, old Fifth..First Sts (= 2nd..6th); lower third blank (masked off, holds fragments of sheet 11). Only Hopper Av junctions, all on one line: helmert.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the area south of Hopper Avenue between First Street (today 6th Street) and Edward Street, down to Berdan Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch. River Road runs through it from Hopper Avenue to Berdan Avenue, bending slightly. West of River Road the Fairlawn Land Improvement Association Map block holds a few dwellings, a stone dwelling, a concrete garage for eighteen cars (heated by steam, lit by electricity) and a row of six small brick stores on River Road; south of it the land along River Road is open, with scattered frame buildings. East of River Road, blocks 128A and 129A along George and Edward Streets are built up near Hopper Avenue with small dwellings and garages, while the southern two thirds are subdivided into narrow numbered lots that are still vacant, lettered as Fairlawn Gardens. Two small offices stand on the River Road frontage near Berdan Avenue. Berdan Avenue is drawn 60 feet wide, Edward Street 40 feet and the others 50 feet.
notes: Old First Street is today's 6th Street; it ends short of Berdan Avenue on the sheet.
Garage for 18 cars on River Road.
50 ft. Hopper Av to Berdan Av, First St (= 6th St), River Rd, George St, Edward St; Fairlawn Gardens lots. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, titled Radburn Section, is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows the first built part of Radburn, the planned community laid out in 1928 and 1929. Along the west edge runs the railroad (E. R. R., the Erie's Bergen County branch) with the Radburn passenger station and a post office, both drawn from plans, beside Fairlawn Avenue. Plaza Road (North Plaza Road, 100 to 105 feet wide) runs north from Fairlawn Avenue; on it stand the Plaza Building, a brick block of stores with a drug store, and a row of two-storey veneered houses, an auto repair garage and garages for up to 25 cars, with lots marked 'Proposed buildings'. East of Plaza Road the superblock between Howard Avenue, High Street and Owen Avenue is drawn with its characteristic cul-de-sac lanes (Burnham, Brighton, Bolton, Burlington, Bancroft, Berkley, Aberdeen, Allen, Arlington, Ashburn and Audubon Places, Brearley Crescent), each with veneered houses facing footpaths ('walk') and interior park strips (parks 4, 7 and 8). Two apartment buildings from plans stand near Abbott Road. North of Owen Avenue, Beekman, Bedford, Bristol and Ballard Places are shown with outlined proposed buildings 'subject to change'. Along the south, High Street and Fairlawn Avenue cross from the railroad to Craig Road, with Addison Place; a future widened line of Fairlawn Avenue is dashed on both sides. Fire alarm boxes are marked.
notes: Drawn at 100 ft to an inch, unlike the 50 ft village sheets.
Berkley Place is Berkeley Place and Brearley Crescent is Brearly Crescent in OpenStreetMap.
Buildings north of Owen Avenue are outlined as proposed and 'subject to change'.
Future line of Fairlawn Avenue is drawn dashed on both sides of the street.
Brighton Place / Plaza Road North was rejected (about 19 m off); the Fairlawn Avenue / Plaza Road and High Street / Plaza Road points are narrow pairs on a street with a planted island.
100 ft. Radburn Section: Plaza Rd, Howard Av, High St, Owen Av, Abbott Rd, Craig Rd, cul-de-sac places; railroad and Radburn station on west edge. One part.

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 8 is the main map, at 100 feet to an inch, covering the Columbia Heights section in the northwest corner of Fair Lawn (the Warren Point district) and the works of the Textile Dyeing Co. of America on the Passaic River. The residential grid runs from Lincoln Avenue on the west, the line with the Borough of Hawthorne, east across Bergen Avenue (today Heights Avenue), Albert Avenue and Pomona Avenue to Smith Avenue, and from Lakeside Avenue at the top past Loretto, Katherine and Columbus Avenues to River (Wagaraw) Road at the bottom. The blocks are lettered as the Columbia Heights Improvement Association Map and are lined with small frame dwellings and garages on narrow lots; a few stores, a drug store and a plumber stand at the Lincoln and Loretto Avenue corner, the Columbia Heights Community Church faces Loretto Avenue, a fire department hose company house stands on Bergen Avenue, and the Lincoln School stands east of Smith Avenue. The east half of the sheet is the Textile Dyeing Co. of America: a large dyeing and finishing building with raised floors, a fireproof printing building built in 1929, a machine shop, tin reclaiming pit, chemical storage, water tanks and fuel oil tanks, beside a long pond, with Maple Avenue along the east edge. Below River Road the Passaic River and the Bergen County line cross the sheet, with a concrete bridge at Lincoln Avenue; the river bank opposite is marked to see the Paterson volume two. The upper right is left blank around an inset (part 2) showing territory also covered on page 208 of the Paterson volume.
notes: Old Bergen Avenue in Columbia Heights is today's Heights Avenue.
River Road west of Maple Avenue is labelled River (Wagaraw) Road; today it is Wagaraw Road.
Textile Dyeing Co. of America works with a fireproof printing building built in 1929.
Sheet notes the territory is also shown on page 208 of the Paterson, N.J. volume 2.

100 ft. Columbia Heights (Lincoln, Bergen = Heights, Albert, Pomona, Smith Avs; Lakeside to Wagaraw Rd) and Textile Dyeing Co. of America; part 2 inset (Harristown Rd to Lakeside Av, the strip north of the main map), also on Paterson vol. 2 p. 208. Drawn at about -12 deg, unlike the village grid.

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 8 is an inset in the upper right of the sheet, framed by heavy lines and drawn at the same 100 feet to an inch, showing the strip of Columbia Heights between Harristown Road and Lakeside Avenue, which lies directly north of the main map. Harristown Road runs diagonally across the top of the inset, with the line of the Borough of Glen Rock drawn along it. From Lincoln Avenue on the west (cut by the frame, with the Paterson volume two noted beyond it) the inset crosses Bergen Avenue (today Heights Avenue), Albert Avenue and Pomona Avenue to Smith Avenue at the right edge; Lakeside Avenue runs along the bottom between Pomona and Smith Avenues. The blocks belong to the Columbia Heights Improvement Association Map and hold scattered frame dwellings, garages and a few vacant lots. Between Pomona and Smith Avenues the Pomona Water Co. has a stand pipe of 185,000 gallons and a pump house. The sheet notes that this territory is also covered on page 208 of the Paterson, N.J. volume 2.
notes: Old Bergen Avenue is today's Heights Avenue.
Pomona Water Co. stand pipe and pump house between Pomona and Smith Avenues.
Inset placed on the sheet away from its true position; it adjoins the north edge of part 1 at Lakeside Avenue.

100 ft. Columbia Heights (Lincoln, Bergen = Heights, Albert, Pomona, Smith Avs; Lakeside to Wagaraw Rd) and Textile Dyeing Co. of America; part 2 inset (Harristown Rd to Lakeside Av, the strip north of the main map), also on Paterson vol. 2 p. 208. Drawn at about -12 deg, unlike the village grid.

sheet-9-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 9 is the main map, at 100 feet to an inch, showing the Henderson Development in the northwest of Fair Lawn, east of Maple Avenue. Maple Avenue runs down the west edge and, near the bottom, bends away to the southwest while its old straight line continues south to Lake Street (today Weber Place). Central Avenue runs north-south through the middle of the tract, and a short street lettered Stowe runs north from Fern Street. The cross streets, from north to south, are Fern Street, Henderson Boulevard, Chester Street, Forest Street, Cedar Street, Oak Street and Lake Street, all drawn 50 feet wide; the blocks are lettered as the Henderson Development map and divided into narrow numbered lots. Development is thin: rows of small one-storey frame dwellings with garages on Fern Street and Henderson Boulevard, scattered houses, coops and sheds elsewhere, a filling station and a store at Maple Avenue and Forest Street, and many vacant lots in the southern blocks. The top of the part is open ground with a cemetery, and the bottom edge shows part of a pond. The east edge is a heavy dividing line running diagonally across the sheet; beyond it lie a detachment around Maple Avenue and River Road (part 2), a strip by the Passaic River between Fairlawn and Hopper Avenues (part 3) and the Fairlawn Fur Co. (not placed).
notes: The straight line of old Maple Avenue south of Oak Street is today's Weber Place; modern Maple Avenue follows the bend to the southwest.
Stowe, a short street north of Fern Street, lies on the line of today's Myrtle Avenue.
Filling station at Maple Avenue and Forest Street.

100 ft. Henderson Development (Maple, Central Avs; Fern to Lake Sts), about -11 deg; part 2 detachment at Maple Av / River Rd (Fabrics Finishing Corp., Wagaraw Block Co., Paterson vol. 2 p. 174), drawn turned; part 3 Fairlawn to Hopper Avs west of old Fifth St (2nd St) by the Passaic, village orientation; part 4 Fairlawn Fur Co. inset unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Fairlawn Fur Co., Inc. (own north arrow, block 126) (no street junction or shared feature; needs a carried point from a placed sheet showing the works, or its position in block 126 relative to sheet-9-3).

sheet-9-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 9 is a detachment in the upper right of the sheet, cut off from the main map by a heavy diagonal line and noted as territory also shown on page 174 of the Paterson, N.J. volume 2. It shows the meeting of Maple Avenue and River Road at the Wagaraw Road corner, ground that lies southwest of the main map and east of the Textile Dyeing Co. on Sheet 8, and it is drawn turned about twelve degrees from the main map. Maple Avenue runs northeast from the corner, and the old line of Maple Avenue (today Weber Place) runs north-south near the top with Lake Street leaving it to the east. Between them stands the Fabrics Finishing Corp'n, Fairlawn Division: a dye house and a two-storey dyeing and finishing building with raised floors, a pump house and storage buildings, with the Glen Club Restaurant beside it. River Road runs southeast across the part past bath houses and sheds by Henderson's Pond, a long pond fed by a stream, to the edge of the sheet. Below River Road the Wagaraw Block Co., makers of cement block, has a large shed with an overhead conveyor.
notes: Detachment drawn at a different orientation from the main map; the sheet notes the territory is also shown on page 174 of the Paterson, N.J. volume 2.
Fabrics Finishing Corp'n, Fairlawn Division, dye works at Maple Avenue and River Road.
Wagaraw Block Co., makers of cement block, on River Road.
Old Maple Avenue north of Lake Street is today's Weber Place.

100 ft. Henderson Development (Maple, Central Avs; Fern to Lake Sts), about -11 deg; part 2 detachment at Maple Av / River Rd (Fabrics Finishing Corp., Wagaraw Block Co., Paterson vol. 2 p. 174), drawn turned; part 3 Fairlawn to Hopper Avs west of old Fifth St (2nd St) by the Passaic, village orientation; part 4 Fairlawn Fur Co. inset unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Fairlawn Fur Co., Inc. (own north arrow, block 126) (no street junction or shared feature; needs a carried point from a placed sheet showing the works, or its position in block 126 relative to sheet-9-3).

sheet-9-3.description: Part 3 of Sheet 9 is a separate block on the right side of the sheet, framed by heavy lines and drawn at 100 feet to an inch but turned to the orientation of the old village sheets. It shows the western edge of the old Fair Lawn village, from Fairlawn Avenue at the top to just below Hopper Avenue, between the Passaic River on the west and Fifth Street (today 2nd Street) along the right edge, which adjoins Sheets 4 and 5. Fairlawn Avenue crosses the river on an iron bridge. East of the river the large block 126 is almost empty, with a concrete block well house and a few frame buildings, while the lots facing Fifth Street are lettered as the Fairlawn Land Improvement Association Map and hold small dwellings, a few stores and sheds. Hopper Avenue crosses near the bottom of the part. West of the river only the bank and the dividing line are drawn.
notes: Old Fifth Street is today's 2nd Street.
Iron bridge carries Fairlawn Avenue over the Passaic River.
Drawn at the village orientation, about 32 degrees from the main map of the sheet.

100 ft. Henderson Development (Maple, Central Avs; Fern to Lake Sts), about -11 deg; part 2 detachment at Maple Av / River Rd (Fabrics Finishing Corp., Wagaraw Block Co., Paterson vol. 2 p. 174), drawn turned; part 3 Fairlawn to Hopper Avs west of old Fifth St (2nd St) by the Passaic, village orientation; part 4 Fairlawn Fur Co. inset unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Fairlawn Fur Co., Inc. (own north arrow, block 126) (no street junction or shared feature; needs a carried point from a placed sheet showing the works, or its position in block 126 relative to sheet-9-3).

sheet-10-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 10 is the main map, at 100 feet to an inch, covering the area east of the old village between Fairlawn Avenue and Berdan Avenue. Along the west edge run Edward Street and the abandoned right of way of the North Jersey Rapid Transit. North of Fairlawn Avenue, Highview Avenue leads up past the Borough Hall and a small park; the rest of that strip is open ground with scattered dwellings, a carpenter shop and an awning and shade manufacturer. South of Fairlawn Avenue the streets running north-south are Arnold Street, Smith Avenue, Hawthorne Avenue, Burbank Street, Lexington Street, Orchard Street and Maple Avenue, crossed by Floral Avenue, Hopper Avenue, Rose Place and Berdan Avenue, with Rosewood Street in the south-west. Most of the blocks are lettered as the Fairlawn Gardens subdivision and cut into narrow numbered lots, many still empty; rows of small frame dwellings line Arnold Street and the streets south of Hopper Avenue, and several houses on Floral Avenue are drawn from plans. The Roosevelt School, of brick with steam heat and electric light, stands on Hopper Avenue at Edward Street. Rose Place, Lexington Street and Maple Avenue are marked not opened in part. A framed inset at the right of the sheet (the Radburn Brick and Supply Co. yard on the Erie Railroad, Bergen County Branch) is drawn over the east side of this part and is not part of it.
notes: Highview Avenue (north of Fairlawn Avenue) and Smith Avenue (south of it) are today's 11th Street, which jogs at Fairlawn Avenue.
Hawthorne Avenue is today's 12th Street.
The abandoned North Jersey Rapid Transit right of way along the west edge is today's Parmelee Avenue.
Borough Hall on Highview Avenue; Roosevelt School on Hopper Avenue.
Rose Place, Lexington Street and Maple Avenue marked not opened in part.

100 ft. Fairlawn Av to Berdan Av, Edward St to Maple Av (Fairlawn Gardens); Highview/Smith = 11th St, Hawthorne = 12th St; Borough Hall, Roosevelt School; part 2 inset Radburn Brick & Supply Co. unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Radburn Brick & Supply Co. yard on the Erie RR Bergen County Branch (no street junction; frame drawn over the main map; needs step 6b from sheet 7 or sheets 12/13 if the yard or track layout is shown there).

sheet-11-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 11 is the main map, at 100 feet to an inch, covering the Bellair Park tract west of River Road in the south of Fair Lawn. The numbered streets Fifth, Sixth, Seventh, Eighth, Ninth, Tenth and Eleventh Streets run north-south and are crossed by Pershing Avenue and Morlot Avenue; River Road runs down the east edge, and in the upper right Berdan Avenue crosses the top of the part between Tenth Street and River Road. Morlot Avenue jogs at River Road, its eastern continuation meeting the road a short way south. The blocks (numbered 140 to 194) are lettered as Bellair Park and laid out in 25 foot lots, many still empty. Development consists of small one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, thickest along Tenth and Eleventh Streets and on Eighth Street south of Morlot Avenue, with a few stores near River Road. Pershing Avenue is marked impassable between Eighth and Ninth Streets. West of Fifth Street, below the heavy dividing line, the Progressive Sand and Gravel Co. has a lot by the Passaic River. The upper left of the sheet is cut off by a heavy line and holds a separately drawn block west of Fifth Street (part 2); Bellair Avenue is labelled where Pershing Avenue continues east of River Road.
notes: Old Pershing Avenue is today's Bellair Avenue.
The old numbered streets are renumbered: old Fifth Street is today's Essex Place, and old Sixth to Eleventh Streets are today's 1st to 6th Streets.
Pershing Avenue marked impassable between Eighth and Ninth Streets.
Morlot Avenue jogs at River Road.
Progressive Sand and Gravel Co. lot by the Passaic River west of Fifth Street.

100 ft. Bellair Park west of River Rd; Pershing Av = Bellair Av; old 5th..11th Sts = Essex Pl, 1st..6th Sts; part 2 detached block old 1st..5th Sts = Arnot, Bush, Canger, Dewey, Essex Pls, Progressive Sand & Gravel pit.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 11 is a block in the upper left of the sheet, cut off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale and orientation, showing the western end of the Bellair Park tract beyond Fifth Street, down to the Passaic River. First, Second, Third, Fourth and Fifth Streets run north-south and are crossed by Pershing Avenue and Morlot Avenue; the north end of the part reaches toward Berdan Avenue. The blocks (numbered 135 to 139 and 152 to 154, with 183 to 186 below Morlot Avenue) are lettered Bellair Park and divided into numbered lots, nearly all vacant: only a few dwellings, sheds and a coop stand on them, and a larger dwelling with a pump house in block 152. The Progressive Sand and Gravel Co. works a sand pit in the north of the part between Fourth and Fifth Streets. The Passaic River runs along the west edge.
notes: Old Pershing Avenue is today's Bellair Avenue.
Old First to Fifth Streets are today's Arnot, Bush, Canger, Dewey and Essex Places.
Progressive Sand and Gravel Co. sand pit.

100 ft. Bellair Park west of River Rd; Pershing Av = Bellair Av; old 5th..11th Sts = Essex Pl, 1st..6th Sts; part 2 detached block old 1st..5th Sts = Arnot, Bush, Canger, Dewey, Essex Pls, Progressive Sand & Gravel pit.

sheet-12-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 12 is the lower left of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, separated from the rest by heavy lines. It continues the Bellair Development east of the part above: Fifteenth Street runs down the west edge and Sixteenth Street through the middle, crossed by Bellair Avenue, Ellis Avenue and Morlot Avenue. The blocks between Bellair and Morlot Avenues are lettered Bellair Development and cut into 25 foot lots, with rows of small one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages along Ellis and Morlot Avenues and many lots still empty; Bellair and Ellis Avenues end at the dividing line on the east, where they are marked as continuing. North of Bellair Avenue the open ground of block 194 holds the Borough of Fairlawn pumping station, with a water tank, pump and a reservoir of 200,000 gallons. South of Morlot Avenue the rest of block 194 is blank. A compass rose stands in the open ground at the bottom.
notes: Old Sixteenth Street is today's 17th Street; old Fifteenth Street keeps its number.
Borough of Fairlawn pumping station and 200,000 gallon reservoir north of Bellair Avenue.

100 ft. Part 1 lower left (old 15th/16th Sts = 15th/17th Sts, pumping station); part 2 upper strip River Rd to 15th St (old 14th = 12th St); part 3 east of the Erie RR (old 18th St = 22nd St, Fairmont Av = Fairmount Pl, Christe/Hartley Pls, Banta Pl, Ward St, Caruth & Williams Co.).

sheet-12-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 12 is the upper third of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, covering the Bellair Development east of River Road between Bellair Avenue and Morlot Avenue. River Road runs down the west edge, with Morlot Avenue meeting it at a jog near the bottom; the cross streets are Thirteenth, Fourteenth and Fifteenth Streets, the last cut by the east edge of the sheet. The Van Rider-Ellis Memorial Church, heated by steam and lit by electricity, stands at the River Road corner at the top left. The large block 162 between River Road and Thirteenth Street is almost empty, with a few dwellings and sheds. East of Thirteenth Street the blocks are lettered Bellair Development and filled with small one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages, several drawn from plans, a plumber shop and a few stores. Below Morlot Avenue a narrow strip of lots on block 194 faces the street, and the heavy dividing line runs across the sheet beneath it.
notes: Old Fourteenth Street is today's 12th Street; old Fifteenth Street keeps its number; old Thirteenth Street has no modern counterpart in the reference data.

sheet-12-3.description: Part 3 of Sheet 12 is the lower right of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, separated by a heavy line, covering the ground on both sides of the Erie Railroad (Bergen County Branch) at the south end of Radburn. Prospect Avenue runs beside the tracks on the west. East of the railroad, Morlot Avenue crosses the part; north of it Fairmont Avenue, Eighteenth Street and Christe Place frame blocks 165 and 166, built up with small frame dwellings and garages, while block 163 between the railroad and Eighteenth Street is empty. South of Morlot Avenue the Caruth and Williams Co., mason supplies and coal, has an office, a coal shed and a wood shed beside the tracks; Banta Place, marked not opened at its north end, and Hartley Place run south to Ward Street, with a few rows of dwellings in blocks 167, 196, 197 and 198.
notes: Old Eighteenth Street is today's 22nd Street; Fairmont Avenue is today's Fairmount Place.

sheet-13-1.description: Part 1 of Sheet 13 is the right half of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, separated from the left half by a heavy stepped line, and covers the Warren Point district east of the Erie Railroad between Winnie Street at the top and Broadway at the bottom. Banta Place, Hartley Place and Grunauer Place run north-south, crossed by Winnie, Raphael and Rosalie Streets and Broadway; Midland Avenue continues the line of Hartley Place south of Broadway, and Banta Place is marked not opened north of Raphael Street. The blocks are lettered as the Grunauer Development and cut into narrow numbered lots, filled in places with small one- and two-storey frame dwellings and garages and elsewhere still vacant. Named buildings include the Fairlawn News printing shop on Hartley Place and the Warren Point Silk Mills on Banta Place near Raphael Street, with stores near Broadway. On the west side of the part, against the dividing line, the Erie Railroad (Bergen County Branch) runs through block 224, where the American Radiator warehouse stands beside the tracks with a wood platform; south of it a few lots of block 239 reach Summit Avenue.
notes: Warren Point Silk Mills and the Fairlawn News printing shop.

sheet-13-2.description: Part 2 of Sheet 13 is the left half of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, separated by a heavy stepped line, covering the southwest corner of Fair Lawn west of the Erie Railroad between Willow Street and Broadway. Cyril Avenue, Kenneth Avenue, Lyncrest Avenue and Summit Avenue run north-south, crossed by Willow Street, Columbia Street, Magnolia Street and Broadway. The borough line with East Paterson runs down the west edge and along Broadway at the bottom, where the Borough of East Paterson is lettered. The blocks south of Willow Street are cut into narrow numbered lots and lettered across their face as the Lyncrest tract; small frame dwellings and garages, a few stores and some concrete block buildings are scattered among many vacant lots. St. Ann's R.C. Church, heated by steam and lit by electricity, stands on Summit Avenue between Magnolia Street and Broadway. North of Willow Street a row of lots fronts the open ground of block 194, which fills the top of the part. A compass rose is drawn in the open ground at the top.
notes: St. Ann's R.C. Church on Summit Avenue.
The line with the Borough of East Paterson (today Elmwood Park) runs along the west edge and Broadway.
